source_checks.conclusion: The successful GUI-thread callback marks pending and attempts scheduling. If the startup thread is still registered, its finished handler removes it and tries again; if finished was handled first, the callback supplies the pending mark and schedules. Both paths retain the same idle predicate.

Background admission stops the pending timer. Active operations, selector identity, queue, running workers and leased payload bytes prevent reclamation. A synchronous initialized receiver can start an action through the unchanged admission path, which stops/coalesces the startup timer instead of trimming during acquisition or upload.

The existing single-shot timeout clears the pending flag after one attempt. Initialization has one callback; later reclamation still requires an existing action/copy mark. Shutdown stops the timer, makes the idle predicate false and suppresses queued replies. The new tests assert no repeat and no post-shutdown attempt.

Failed initialization leaves pending false and preserves its existing error/initialized signal behavior. The only new product behavior is inside __GLIBC__; other platforms retain the existing callback behavior.

Four added tests cover successful one-pass startup, failed initialization, shutdown and a deliberately held background worker. Existing tests cover pending upload, selector, post-use cleanup and cancellation. The held-worker scope guard releases its promise before OperationService destruction even when an assertion returns early. These assertions verify attempted cleanup and scheduling, not an RSS saving.

Only the two approved files differ from the reviewed baseline. The product change reuses the existing two-second quiet timer and allocator call; it adds no recurring timer, allocator configuration, cache teardown, provider change or native UI change.
